[quote=dhornaper;60505923][B]Dhornaper - State of Affairs[/b]

More than two years had passed since Fereydun Khan had overthrown Kouroush Parviz' government. Since then, he had consolidated control over the state, appointing loyalists and controlling his more freewheeling Ministers with direct interventions into their Ministries.

The old political parties were forced to accept a supervisor to ensure their activities and finances were legal or be outlawed. The old political elite were, for the most part, co-opted into the new tricameral system, which left all power concentrated in his hand-picked senate anyway, or bribed into retirement with comfortable pensions in return for public support. For the remaining few who opposed Fereydun Khan, they were either intimidated by being silenced under gag laws and suspended in lengthy and intensive investigations, outright imprisoned, or fled into exile when opposition became untenable.

The traditional media too had been brought under control. Dhornaper's state news network had been put under tight watch by censors since the first days of the coup while other large news agencies had censors embedded into their editorial teams. New age media had been more of a challenge to control. Some measures had been put in place, such as state-sponsored forums and groups that harass and doxx critics while the police would track down and force social media users into deleting posts under defamation laws. The result on opposition in the internet has been less successful but the Ministry of Interior is working on increasing its efforts.

The benefits of his autocratic rule so far had outweighed the costs in political freedom. Unemployment is decreasing, the economy is growing, inflation is at an acceptable level, crime is low, construction projects were being worked on, and the propaganda efforts had successfully painted a picture of the nation getting more done than the old democratic system. For the time being, public support is with Fereydun Khan.[/quote]

[B]A Plebiscite for Life Presidency[/b]

The successes of Fereydun Khan's two years as President the constant propaganda drive, and the assassination attempt had led to well crafted calls from journalists to call for Fereydun Khan to have his Presidency "extended". These calls in the media and the general political backdoor talk from Fereydun Khan's loyalists resulted in the idea forming that he should be compensated appropriately for his achievements.

The result of this was the Presidents of both the Council and House of Representatives appealed to the Senate to "compensate" Fereydun Khan "in a manner that fits his achievements". The Senate obliged and although some of Fereydun Khan's senators and Ministers demurred at the proposal of granting him a life Presidency and letting him pick his successor, they were outnumbered.

When the Senate's vote was brought to Fereydun Khan, he refused to accept it and, after a carefully choreographed back-and-forth, he feigned a reluctant acceptance of being President for life if a plebiscite approved it but adamantly rejected being able to pick his successor.

The answer was returned back to the Senate which had the voting commission speedily arrange a plebiscite the next week. The vote had a simple question:

"Do you agree that Fereydun Khan should become President for life?"

[quote=democratic_sanguivallis;60505455][b]Great Red Embassy[/b]

For all of Sanguivallis's quiet difference to the geopolitical objectives of Qianxun, it's easy to miss that it is in fact the senior partner in more ways than one. Surrounded by neighbors susceptible to the revolution, with a modernized military, good standards of living, and immense cultural prestige, the Sanguinian nation effectively stands far above the historically isolationist Qianxun as the most likely flagbearer of communist revolution. However, Pio Graci and his so-called "Red triumvirate" has not yet put this immense diplomatic weight into practice, their only action of any notable importance being the deployment of the Shamatine Assault Flotilla to safeguard International interests in Astanir.

Things have changed, however. With the Social Renaissance Party "now certain" that communist victory in Astanir seemed all but inevitable, Pio Graci would be convinced by his advisors to also search for his own independent pursuits on Elseyr.

The premier power on the continent at this moment was the Elseyran Defense Union, a neo-imperialist product of the liberal international order. They will be the Socialist International's main enemy on Elseyr, and thus Pio Graci would immediately initiate a series of steps to protect the International and the global revolution entire through a massive diplomatic undertaking that he called the "Great Red Embassy", which would target nations that the SRP Patriciate would deem to be "potentially friendly" to Sanguivallis's communist regime. A secondary mission, the "Little Red Embassy", would also be started at the lower level to foster economic ties with nations beyond Elseyr.

[b]Mission to Montfleur[/b]

To begin, Pio Graci would send his largest delegation to the Kingdom of Montfleur, a nation in West Elseyr chiefly famous for its democratic socialism. While such ideological practices run contrary to the Socialist International's own statement of policies and would be intolerable to the inflexible Qianxun, the Sanguinians would be far more forthcoming, believing that Montfleurois socialism could be effectively pushed towards Renaissance Socialism given enough time and persuasion.

Argo Lo Pilato, the head of the SRP Patriciate, would be sent to represent the Sanguinian government at Montfleur, bringing together with him an entourage of religious scholars and socialist theoreticians to possibly undertake an anthropological study of the Montfleurois nation. On paper, the mission would be an exclusively economic pursuit to restore any ties that may have been lost by the Sanguinians during the Palace Revolution, though it was rather clear that given sufficient ability, the Sanguinians will spare no expense to drag the Montfleurois into the Socialist International's fold.

[b]Mission to Gythena[/b]

Overlooking the great Arctic was the Commonwealth of Gythena, a neutral Elseyran state embedded deep into EDU territory, flanked to its south and east by neo-imperialist states. And yet, the Gythenians lived beyond their spheres of influence, its politics manifestly isolationist. Though Pio Graci would have some reservations on Gythena's actual capacity for a people's democratic revolution, he would nevertheless trust the Patriciate's judgement and would sent for a smaller diplomatic mission under Menelao Impastato, Rector of Sanguivallis.

Unlike with the Montfleur delegation, the Sanguinians would restrain themselves in Gythena to avoid alarming the EDU, with Impastato being given explicit orders to only steer talks with the Gythenians in strictly economic and cultural matters such as the creation of comprehensive trade agreements, cultural and student exchange programs, and other non-military bilateral agreements. To further remove its military presence, Pio Graci would enlist the help of MROS Dynamics, a Vespurian PMC, to serve as official guards for the Sanguinian delegation.

[b]Little Red Embassies[/b]

The states of Arenenge, Lavia, Nordiheim, Vespurias, Thrysmora, Bob, Hydronia, Apollonia, and Sikirsk would all be identified as potential "Little Red Embassy" targets, with Sanguivallis sending delegations to all of these nations to gauge their willingness for international cooperation with the Sanguinian Democratic Republic. Pio Graci himself would be the coordinator of these meetings, setting agendas for each and every delegation, and tracking the specific grievances and interpretations that each nation state may provide from Sanguinian overtures.

While the specific arrangements for each nation would not be listed here for brevity, in general the Sanguinians would simply request for the creation of comprehensive free trade agreements with each little red embassy, which may involve the setting of maximum tarriff rates on various goods and services, simplifying barriers for foreign direct investments, research and development collaboration, and environmental partnerships. The specifics of these provisions may be debated to account for the cultural and geopolitical sensitivities of each nation state listed.[/quote]
[b]The Sanguivallians[/b]

Cardinal Jean-luc Rochambeau stood on the docks of Gvenchy-Sur-Prade, his red robes whipped aside by the winds that day. It was ironic that he had been chosen by king Henri to be the one to meet the Sanguivallian communist delegation.

Monsieur Rochambeau, stated a voice behind him, causing him to turn to face the speaker, it was Secretary Villiarde, vice chairman of Li Baptistes.

Ah Mssr. Villiarde, an honour, replied Rochambeau, moving to shake the hand of Villiarde.

So it is, so it is, replied Villiarde with a thin smile, his gaze fixed out to the entrance of the docks, where in the distance a small flotilla began to appear.

I assume the chairman sent you? Enquired the cardinal.

Yes, he wants us to determine exactly what type of communists these sanguivallians are, see if we might be able to reconcile our differences, replied Villiarde.

Well I wish us the best, because here they come! Replied to cardinal, with a sweep of his hand towards the approaching flotilla. The stage was set, now what would become of the matter is a story to come.

[b]And they came like lightning, and the lightning was strange[/b]

And the boats did moor to port swiftly, like they were being pulled to it by ropes, and so did the men disembark just as quickly. Red hair. The first thing the Montfleurois would notice was the strange, spiky red hair of a certain man in the Sanguinian delegation. This man who set the pace of all the other Sanguinan delegates was a rather tall apparatcik, pale-skinned, dressed in the artillery uniform of the old tradition, with reddish hair that figured prominently in the bright blue sky.

"Argo Lo Pilato" he said to the Montfleurois, extending an arm to them, his face somewhere between apathetic and bemused by the extravagant display of the Cardinal's attire and Gvenchy-Sur-Prade's architecture. "In my homeland, I am the Chairman of the Standing Council for the Patriciate, which is no title used by most liberal governments. Mr. Lo Pilato shall therefore suffice as my manner of address."

After Argo, there was another oddity. A woman who stood immediately behind Argo, wearing a strange black suit jacket style that seem more like a biker's jacket than a formal dress, with matching black gloves, boots, even armbands that almost looked more like bracers or gauntlets. More strangely, however, was her use of a pair of thick black sunglasses that completely obscured her facial expression. Judging by her odd demeanor, she had to have been Argo's second-in-command.

"Yo. Immacolata Terrasi." She said, introducing herself casually after Argo, though not extending a hand herself, standing a bit too far for the motion to look natural. "Chairwoman of the Socialist Renaissance Party Central Commission for Foreign Trade and Commerce. Ms. Terrasi will do though. Imma too, actually!"

"Just Ms. Terrasi, please." Argo corrected, nudging his second-in-command carefully with an elbow.

[b]Initial Impressions[/b]
Rochambeau and Villiard would both greet the newcomers with a diplomatic politeness that rivaled perhaps even the most astute politician. Rochambeau would speak first.

Greetings Mr. Lo Pilato, and Ms. Terrasi, it is an honour to have you here in Montfleur. My name is Cardinal Jean-Luc-Rochambeau, though Monseignur Rochambeau would be preferred, he then turned to Villiard, nodding for him to speak, which he did, with a bow.

I extend the same greetings to you, I am Mssr. Villiard, vice-chairman of the Communist Party of Montfleur, chairman Lucarde sends his regards.

With pleasantries exchanged the cardinal would step towards the line of waiting black cars that sat on the road along the dock, leading the way, with Mssr. Villiard moving behind him, yet another sign of the Montfleurois preference for politeness and deference to authority. 

The scene would be perhaps odd to the foreign observer, the Montfleurois gave no impression of distaste or taste for their guests, nor could one ascertain the opinions of the two gentlemen from the way they spoke or even moved their guests along, though in reality the two Montfleurois were a tad bit unsure about their odd guests.
